searchText: It would be valuable to add JSON-RPC changes for Berlin, but it isn't strictly required as JSON-RPC isn't consensus. IMO adding consensus level changes without giving users the tools to inspect them sets a bad precedent. For example if a users sends an EIP-2930 tx but their access list doesn't show up in EtherScan it could lead to confusion for the user if they sent the tx correctly. In the case of 2930, the vast majority of users won't actually need the new feature. It is there primarily so that **if** someone's stuff breaks there is a way to fix it. Those 2 to 3 fields are fairly easy to add. At least easier than the over-the-wire encoding of typed transactions. I think all clients can ship them with their block number updates (when we pick a block #) I will make a change for type to become quantity, it is more consistent then having it as int. There are some examples of `number` in the protocol I believe. And in general I think it would be nice to move that direction. Hmm, it does seem that `number` is fairly uncommon. Yea, for me number was more intuition and better fit, but it seems sequence is more widely used and it is better to continue having consistence for same expectation. Your argument is compelling, even if it makes me sad. EIP 2718 describes all the transaction types in hex, so Quantity makes it read the same in JSON-RPC. The inconsistency that bothers me is how block numbers are returned or parameterized in hex in JSON-RPC but EIPs and chain configs use decimal.
